page: Microsoft Azure D48lds_v6 is a compute-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Dldsv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 260 MB of L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). The server is configured with 96.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It also includes 2835 GB of local NVMe SSD storage.

Benchmark results indicate strong performance across compute, memory, and storage operations. The server achieved a PassMark CPU score of 63378.89 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 20188.0. Memory bandwidth tests show strong throughput, reaching 3685.22 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 255.6 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. In database and web serving tests, the instance demonstrated strong capabilities, processing 67.02 million Redis SET operations per second and delivering 81.17 GB/sec of static web serving throughput. Image processing performance is classified as top-tier, scoring 20858.0 on Geekbench.

The primary tradeoff of the D48lds_v6 is its low memory density of 2.0 GB per vCPU, which limits its suitability for memory-intensive applications. However, this configuration offers qualitative cost efficiency for compute-heavy workloads that do not require large memory footprints, as users avoid paying for unneeded RAM. The inclusion of 2835 GB of local NVMe SSD storage provides high-speed local disk access. This server is suited for workloads such as software compilation, image processing, web serving, and database operations that benefit from high CPU clock speeds and fast local storage rather than massive memory capacity.
